blocks.text: I can write a plan for the first paragraph of a diary entry.
You will pretend to be the girl in ‘The Journey’. First you will retell her journey out loud, then you will write your plan in notes.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: Speaking aloud to retell events that have already happened.
The point of view where the speaker or writer is the ‘I’ character, giving a personal account of events or experiences.
A framework that writers create before they write a section or a whole text.

slides.title: The shape of our diary entry

blocks.text: Our diary entry will be built like this:

items: the date
the greeting: ‘Dear Diary,’
paragraph 1: a recount of the journey
paragraph 2: expressing current feelings
the sign-off

blocks.text: Today we are planning {paragraph 1}, the recount of the journey.
**Perspective** is the way someone thinks, feels or sees something. It is their point of view. These people are speaking from the first person perspective, as ‘I’:

items: I love to play with my friends!
My favourite subject is geography.
I can see a park on the map.

blocks.text: When you write your diary entry, you pretend to be the girl. You write ‘I did this’ or ‘I felt this’, not ‘she felt this’. Writing from a character’s perspective means expressing their thoughts and feelings.

items.q: Which sentence is written in first person perspective?
options: I felt terrified in the forest.
She felt terrified in the forest.
The girl felt terrified in the forest.

items.q: When you write from a character’s perspective, you are …
options: writing lots of facts
expressing the character’s thoughts and feelings
describing the pictures

slides.title: Oral recount: the five key moments

blocks.text: An {oral recount} helps us understand the **chronology**, the order of events. Here is what happened, in order:

items: 1. Their mother told them to pack their bags and say goodbye to their home.
2. They travelled for many days until they arrived at the border, where they were turned away by the security guard.
3. They ran away from the border police and hid overnight in the forest.
4. They crossed a vast sea on a ferry packed with other refugees.
5. They took a train through many countries and travelled closer to their new, safe home.

blocks.text: Try it aloud, speaking as the girl: ‘My mother told us to pack our bags and say goodbye to our home …’
At each moment, think about her emotions. Tap the ideas below to see the words you could use.

blocks.q: Put each feeling word with the moment when the girl might feel it.
Choose the thought that fits each moment.

items.q: The moment they cross the sea on the crowded ferry.
options: My stomach was churning violently!
I don’t want to leave! What about my toys?
I am so relieved to be closer to our new home.

items.q: The moment they are turned away at the border after many days of travel.
options: I am so relieved to be sitting on the train.
It was so exciting!
My legs were aching and I was desperate for a break.

items.q: The moment they are on the train, closer to safety.
options: I didn’t want to say goodbye to my toys!
I am so relieved to be sitting down and closer to our new home.
I couldn’t sleep because I was so terrified.

blocks.text: A {plan} helps the writer summarise and organise key information. It uses **notes**.

items: Notes are short. They capture the most important information.
For a diary entry, that means the key events in chronological order, plus thoughts and feelings.
We do not write in full sentences.
We use bullet points.

blocks.text: Take a full sentence and pull out the key words and phrases.
Full sentence: ‘We ran away from the border police and hid in the forest all night.’

items: ran away from border police
hid in forest overnight

blocks.label: What did we do?
blocks.text: We kept the key events and left out the extra words. Each note is short, and there are no capital letters or full stops needed.

slides.title: Which one belongs in a plan?

items.q: Which is the best note for: ‘We crossed the sea on a ferry that was packed with other refugees.’
options: We crossed the sea on a ferry that was packed with other refugees.
crossed sea on ferry
sea

items.q: Which does NOT belong in a plan?
options: key events in time order
thoughts and feelings
long full sentences with capital letters and full stops

items.q: How should notes for a diary plan be organised?
options: in any order
as bullet points in time order
in one long sentence

blocks.text: Notes for paragraph 1, from leaving their country until they arrive at the boat. Here is a model:

items: packed all our belongings
said goodbye to everyone
travelled for many days and nights
turned away at border
ran away from the border police
spent the night in the forest

blocks.text: And some thoughts and feelings to add:

items: my heart was pounding
hugged Mumma tightly all night
my legs were aching
shattered / exhausted
I was heartbroken
Why must everything change?

slides.title: Plan: the boat to the train

blocks.text: Notes for the second part of paragraph 1, from the boat journey until they were on the train. Here is a model:

items: crossed the sea on a ferry
spoke to other passengers
took a train across many countries
arrived closer to a safe place

blocks.text: And some thoughts and feelings to add:

items: seasick / nauseous
legs like jelly
relieved and hopeful
miss my friends and toys

blocks.q: Sort each note into a key event or a thought or feeling.

items.text: ran away from the border police
crossed the sea on a ferry

items: An oral recount, saying the events out loud in order, helps us understand the chronology.
We plan and rehearse in the first person, from the girl’s perspective.
A good plan has key events in chronological order and thoughts and feelings.
The plan is written as notes, using bullet points for the most important information.
Paragraph 1 recounts the events of the journey in order, starting from when the family left home.

flashcards.back: Speaking aloud to retell events that have already happened.

The point of view where the speaker or writer is the ‘I’ character, giving a personal account.

Example: I love to play with my friends!
A framework that writers create before they write a section or a whole text.

flashcards.front: Why do we do an oral recount before we plan?
flashcards.back: It makes sure we have a clear understanding of the chronology (order) of events.

flashcards.front: Which perspective do we use when planning our diary entry?
flashcards.back: First person, as the girl in ‘The Journey’.

flashcards.front: What does a good plan for a diary entry include?
flashcards.back: Key events in chronological order, and thoughts and feelings.
As notes, using bullet points to capture the most important information. We do not use full sentences.

flashcards.front: What does paragraph 1 of the diary entry do?
flashcards.back: It recounts the events from the journey in chronological order, starting from when the family left home.

flashcards.front: What does paragraph 2 of the diary entry do?
flashcards.back: It expresses the writer’s current feelings.

flashcards.front: How might the girl feel while she says goodbye to her home?
How might the girl feel while hiding in the forest overnight?
flashcards.back: Scared, but also brave and proud.

flashcards.front: How might the girl feel on the train, closer to safety?

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Planning the first paragraph of a diary entry
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a word or a short phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the word for speaking aloud to retell events that have already happened?
questions.explanation: An oral recount is speaking aloud to retell events that have already happened.

questions.prompt: What is the word for a framework that writers create before they write a section or a whole text?
questions.explanation: A plan is a framework that writers create before they write.

questions.prompt: Which point of view uses ‘I’: first person, second person or third person?
questions.explanation: First person perspective is where the writer is the ‘I’ character.

questions.prompt: Is a plan written in full sentences or in notes?
questions.explanation: A plan is written in note format to capture the most important information.

questions.prompt: What do we use to list each note in our plan?
questions.explanation: A plan uses bullet points to capture the most important information.

questions.prompt: In what order should the events in your plan be written?
questions.explanation: Key events go in chronological order, the order they happened.

questions.prompt: Which paragraph of the diary entry expresses the writer’s current feelings: paragraph 1 or paragraph 2?
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 is the recount of the journey and paragraph 2 expresses current feelings.

questions.prompt: A good diary plan includes key events in chronological order and what else?
questions.explanation: An effective plan contains key events in chronological order and thoughts and feelings.
